sections.h2: Windsor, two counties and a fast-growing town
sections.html:
Windsor, a home rule town in Northern Colorado, straddles the Weld and Larimer county line. It was platted in 1882 and incorporated on April 2, 1890, and it sits at 4,797 feet across about 26 square miles. The older core runs along State Highway 392, which doubles as Main Street, with the original street grid stretching roughly six blocks north and south of it. The Cache la Poudre River bends past the western and southern sides, and old gravel pits along its banks have become lakes ringed by houses and a golf course.

Annexation in the 1990s pushed the limits west into Larimer County, and the part of town beyond Interstate 25 now touches Loveland. A house on the Larimer side is recorded and taxed through different county offices than one on the Weld side, so settle the county first.

sections.h2: Growth, housing age and who buys here
sections.html:
The population went from 4,277 in 1980 to 32,716 in the 2020 census, and the 2025 estimate is 43,840. The 2020 count showed 11,807 households and 12,846 housing units, with 8.1% of the units vacant. The median age was 38.2, and 65.9% of households were married-couple households.

Those numbers describe a family suburb that filled in through successive subdivisions. Two Windsor houses can be far apart in the age of the roof, siding and furnace. Windsor sits between Fort Collins and Greeley, with Loveland close on the west. Many buyers work in one of those cities and choose Windsor for the lot size or newer construction. Weld RE-4 is the school district for most of town, and the district is the right source when a buyer asks about a particular school.

sections.h2: How do hail and tornadoes affect a Windsor sale?
sections.html:
Hail is the weather event that most often affects a Windsor sale. The town typically sees 6 to 12 hail days a year, and the area where Colorado, Nebraska and Wyoming meet gets more hail than any other place in the country. On May 22, 2008, a tornado hit Windsor and parts of Weld and Larimer counties, with pockets of EF3 damage, estimated winds up to 165 mph and hail as large as baseballs. It caused $193.5 million in damage from about 24,000 auto and homeowner claims.

  • Old hail damage on a roof is something the buyer's inspector will probably flag.
  • A lender or insurer reviewing the house may ask about claim history.
  • Daily temperature swings can top 50 degrees Fahrenheit in spring and fall, which is hard on exterior paint, sealant and concrete.

Someone paying cash accepts the house in its present state, so a hail-worn roof need not be replaced before closing, which is a common question from owners with storm damage.

sections.h2: Building permits and repairs in Windsor
sections.html:
Windsor has its own permit desk at 200 N. 11th Street, staffed for walk-ins Monday through Thursday, with online services handling Fridays. New building plans are reviewed under the 2024 I-Codes, and the town follows the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. Homeowner handouts cover re-roofs, decks, basement finishes, patio covers and pools.

Contractor licenseNo contractor license is required for work inside the Town
Electrical and plumbingContractors must hold a current State of Colorado license
Permit expirationPermits expire if work does not begin within 180 days or stops for 180 days

Inspection requestsRequests by 3:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday are scheduled for the next working day
Permit desk phone970-674-2436

The town's Homeowners Resource Center has HOA information and a wildfire code map, and owners should check that map and ask their insurer about any wildfire-related requirements. Work that was started without a finished permit is better sorted out with the permit technician now than discovered later by someone else's inspector.

sections.h2: Recording a deed on the Weld County side
sections.html: Deeds for Weld County addresses go to the Clerk and Recorder at 1250 H Street in Greeley. The office charges $43.00 for a letter or legal size document, however many pages it has. On top of that sits the state's documentary fee of $.01 per $100 of sale price, owed when the price is over $500. The county's fee page lists both, and the title company normally pays them at closing. Larimer County parcels use that county's own recording office instead.

sections.h2: Property taxes when a Windsor house sells
sections.html:
Weld County parcels owe the prior year's tax as of January 1. You may split it into two equal installments or pay once. The posted dates are February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second and April 30 for a single payment. Late interest starts at 1% and rises month by month.

Title companies confirm that nothing is owed by requesting a Certificate of Taxes Due from the Treasurer. The Treasurer's tax information page has the full schedule.

Bills are addressed to the owner of record. A seller who has already moved should verify the mailing address the county holds, so a notice is not lost mid-sale. Forward any bill you do receive to the title company right away, so it can be settled from the proceeds.

sections.h2: Listing, selling yourself or taking a cash offer
sections.html:
You can sell a Windsor house three ways, and each runs on its own clock. Condition and urgency usually decide it.

  • Through an agent: expect showings, a buyer's loan and appraisal, and a repair list from the inspector.
  • By yourself: marketing, contracts and disclosures fall to you, and a title company is still needed.
  • For cash: the house sells as is, and a title company closes it on a date you can live with.

Owners who inherited a Windsor house, are behind on payments, have tenants in place or are sitting on hail damage tend to look at the third route. Send the address through the form on this page and we will reply with a written cash offer, with no obligation.

Before you decide, find out which county your parcel is in, collect your latest tax notice, and list any open permits. Those three facts shape every other step, from which office records the deed to what the title company needs from you.

A short timeline helps too. The buyer visits, an offer follows, and the title company opens its file and orders a Certificate of Taxes Due. You sign the deed at closing, and the Clerk and Recorder or the Larimer County equivalent records it. If a hail claim is pending with your insurer, mention it at the start, since it affects who is paid for the roof.

faqs.q: Is Windsor, CO in Weld County or Larimer County?
faqs.a: Both. Windsor lies in Weld and Larimer counties, and the town limits were extended west into Larimer County in the 1990s.

faqs.q: How many people live in Windsor, Colorado?
faqs.a: The census counted 32,716 residents in 2020, and the estimate for 2025 is 43,840.

faqs.q: Does Windsor require a contractor license for repairs before I sell?
faqs.a: No contractor license is required for work inside the Town, although electrical and plumbing contractors must hold a state license. Most projects still need a building permit.

faqs.q: When are Weld County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Tax is due January 1 for the previous year. The county's dates are February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for a single full payment.

faqs.q: Can I sell a hail-damaged house in Windsor without replacing the roof?
faqs.a: Yes, if the buyer agrees to take it as is. A cash buyer does not require a new roof first, while a financed buyer's lender or insurer may ask for repairs.
